Collection/Calacatta Oro
N° 01 / 08

calacatta oro

[ 01 ] — Character

A bright white ground, crossed by broad veins that run from soft grey into gold.

Calacatta Oro is quarried in the Apuan Alps above Carrara, and it is far scarcer than the Carrara marble that shares its mountains. The veins are few and bold, so each slab reads as a single drawing — which is why it is so often book-matched across a wall.

Origin
Apuan Alps, Tuscany, Italy
Stone
Marble
Ground
Bright white
Veining
Broad and bold, grey into gold
Finishes
Polished, honed, brushed, bush-hammered
Formats
Slabs, tiles, cut-to-size

[ 04 ] — Laying it out

Open the block like a book.

Slabs sawn one after another from the same block carry the same vein. How they are laid decides the drawing on the wall.

[ 05 ] — Where it works

Rooms it was made for.

  • 01

    Feature walls

    Book-matched pairs turn the vein into the centrepiece.

  • 02

    Worktops and islands

    Seal it, and wipe citrus or wine promptly: marble is sensitive to acids.

  • 03

    Bathrooms

    Vanity tops, shower walls and floors.

  • 04

    Floors

    Honed, for a softer sheen and a surer step.

  • 05

    Stairs and sills

    Cut to size, with the vein carried from tread to tread.

  • 06

    Fireplaces and furniture

    Surrounds, table tops and shelves.
